translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the churches of God that are in Corinth, with all the saints who are in all Achaia:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all consolation,
who comforts us in all our afflictions, so that we too may be able to comfort all those who are afflicted with that comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
for just as the sufferings of Christ abound toward us, so also through Christ our consolations abound.
For whether we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is brought about through the endurance of those same sufferings that we also suffer. And our hope for you is firm.
Or if we are consoled, it is for your consolation and salvation; we know that just as you are sharers in our sufferings, so also are you in the consolation.
For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, about our affliction that befell us in Asia; for we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our strength, to the point of giving up even on our life.
Indeed, we ourselves received the sentence of death in ourselves, so that we might not trust in ourselves but in God, who raises the dead,
who delivered us from such a death and delivers us, and in whom we hope that he will deliver us yet again,
with the help of your prayers for us, so that the grace granted to us through many persons may become, through many, an occasion of thanksgiving on your behalf.

For this is our boast, the testimony of our mind: that in sincerity and the truth of God, and not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in the world, and all the more toward you.
For we write nothing else to you except what you read and what you have come to know; and I hope that you will understand it fully as well,
just as you have come to know us from time to time, that we are your boast, as you are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And with this hope I wished to come to you first, so that you might have a second joy,
and to go from you to Macedonia, and to come back to you again from Macedonia, and to be sent on by you to Judea.
So when I planned this, could I have counted it a small matter? Or what I plan, do I plan in some fleshly way, so that with me there should be yes, yes and no, no?
But God is faithful, for our word to you was not yes and no.
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you through us, by me and Timothy and Silvanus, was not yes and no, but in him the yes has come to be.
For as many as are the promises of God, in him is the yes and in him the amen, to the glory of God through us.
It is God who has established us with you in Christ and has anointed us;
and he has sealed us and given us the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
But I call upon God as witness against my soul that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy, for you stand by faith.
And I decided this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.
For if I grieve you, then who is it that will gladden me, if not the one who has been grieved by me?
And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I come I may not have grief from those from whom I ought to have joy; I trust in all of you, that my joy is the joy of all of you.
For out of much grief and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be grieved, but that you should know the surpassing love that I have toward you.
But if anyone has grieved me, he has not grieved me, but in some measure (so as not to burden you) all of you.
This rebuke by the many is enough.
But now, on the contrary, you should rather forgive and comfort him, lest such a person be swallowed up by excessive grief.
Therefore I beseech you to confirm your love toward him.
For this is why I wrote, that I might know your proven character, whether you are obedient in everything.
And whatever you forgive me, I also forgive; for indeed, whatever I too have forgiven, I have forgiven for your sake before the face of Christ,
so that we may not be taken advantage of by the devil, for we are not ignorant of his mind.
Now when I came to Troas with the gospel of Christ, and a door was opened to me by the Lord,
I had no rest for my spirit, because I did not find Titus, my brother; but I took leave of them and went out to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always makes us manifest through Christ and reveals through us in every place the scent of the knowledge of him.
For we are the fragrances of Christ from God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing:
to some a scent of death leading to death, and to others a scent of life leading to life. And who is capable of this?
For we are not, like the many, traders in the word of God; but as from earnest desire, indeed as from God, before God, we speak through Christ.
Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as some do, a letter of commendation to you, or likewise one of commendation from you?
Or are you not our letter from the Lord, written in our hearts, known and read by all people?

It has been made known that you are an apostolic letter of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of the heart of flesh.
And such is the hope we have through Christ toward God.
Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to count anything as coming from us; rather, our sufficiency is from God,
It is he who has made us capable of serving a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit, for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

Now if that ministry of death, engraved in letters on tablets, became glorious, so that the children of Israel could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, which was passing away,
how much more will the ministry of the Spirit be in glory?
For if the ministry of condemnation is glory, how much more will the ministry of righteousness surpass it in glory.
For indeed, what was glorified is no longer glorified in this respect, because of the glory that surpasses it.
For if what was passing away was in glory, how much more is what endures in glory.
Since, then, we have such a hope, let us use great openness.
And not as Moses, who put a veil over his face, so that the children of Israel might not look upon the end of that which was passing away.
But their minds were blinded, for until this very day the same veil remains unremoved upon the reading of the old law, for it is done away through Christ.
But until this very day, whenever Moses is read aloud, a veil lies upon their heart.
But when one turns to the Lord, that veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And all of us, with unveiled face, behold the glory of the Lord, and we are being changed into that same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.
Therefore we have this ministry, as we have been shown mercy, and we do not lose heart,

but we have put away the hidden things of shame, and we do not walk in craftiness, nor do we deal deceitfully with the word of God, but by the open declaration of the truth we commend ourselves to every human mind before God.
And if this gospel of ours is hidden, it is hidden among those who are perishing,
whose unbelieving minds the god of this world has blinded, so that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of the invisible God, might not shine upon them.
For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord, and ourselves as your servants for the sake of Jesus.
For God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, who has shone in our hearts for the enlightenment of the knowledge of the glory of God before the face of Jesus Christ.
But we have this treasure in vessels of clay, so that the surpassing greatness of the power may be of God and not from us.
In everything we are afflicted, but it does not seem to us confinement; though we are given up for lost, yet it does not seem to us abandonment;
though we are persecuted, we are not forsaken; though we are struck down, we are not destroyed.
always we carry the death of the Lord Jesus in these bodies of ours, so that the life of Jesus also may be revealed in these bodies of ours.
For always we, the living, are given over to death for the sake of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be revealed in these mortal bodies of ours;
so that death is at work in us, but life among you.
And we have the same spirit of faith, as it is written: I believed, and therefore I spoke; and we too believe, and therefore we speak.
We know this, that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also through Jesus, and will present us together with you.
For all things are for your sake, so that the grace may abound through the many, and the thanksgiving may overflow to the glory of God.
Therefore we do not lose heart, but though this outer man of ours is decaying, yet the inner man is renewed day by day.
For this momentary small affliction of ours produces for us an exceeding and surpassing great eternal glory.
For we do not look at what is visible, but at what is invisible, for what is visible is temporary, but what is invisible is eternal.
For we know that if this earthly house, our dwelling, is destroyed, we have a house built by God, not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.
And because of this we groan, and we long to put on our dwelling from heaven,
If we put it on, we shall no longer be found naked.
For we who are in this dwelling groan and are weighed down, because we do not wish to be stripped, but to be clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
But he who created us for this very thing is God, who gave us the pledge of the Spirit.
We are therefore always confident, and we know that we have come in by this flesh and are gone out from the Lord.
For we conduct ourselves by faith and not by conjecture.
But we dare, and we think it better rather to go out from this flesh and to go to the Lord.
For this reason too we are honored, whether we come in or go out, if only we may be pleasing to him.
For all of us are to be revealed before the throne of Christ, so that each one may receive from this flesh what he has done, whether good or evil.
Therefore we know, we know the fear of the Lord; shall we then persuade people? For before God we are revealed, and we trust that we are revealed also to your minds.

And it is not that we again commend ourselves to you, but we give you occasion for boasting on our account, so that you may have it toward those who boast only before the face and not also in the heart.
For whether we were out of our senses, it was for God; or whether we have become wise, it is for you.
For the love of Christ urges us to discern this: that one died for all, and so all have died.
And he died for all, so that those who live may no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and rose for them.
From now on we no longer know anyone according to the flesh; for even if we knew Christ according to the flesh, yet now we no longer know him.
But whatever is through Christ is a new creation; the first has passed away; behold, everything has become new.
And everything is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ Jesus and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
For God was with Christ, reconciling the world to himself and not counting their sins against them, and he placed with us the word of reconciliation.
Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as God entreats you through us; we beseech you for Christ's sake: be reconciled to God.
For he who did not know sin, he made sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.
And we help you and entreat you that you not receive the grace of God in vain.
For he says: In the time of acceptance I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you. Behold, now is the time of acceptance; behold, now is the day of salvation.
Let none of you, in anything, give even one stumbling block to anyone, so that this ministry of yours may not be reproached.
But in everything present yourselves as servants of God, with much patience, in afflictions and griefs, in distresses
and torments, in imprisonments and tumults, with labor and watchfulness, with fasting
and purity, with knowledge and long-suffering, with sweetness and the Holy Spirit, with unfeigned love,
with the word of truth, with the power of God, with the weapon of righteousness of the right hand and of the left,
through honour and dishonour, through slander and praise; treated as deceivers, and yet true;
as unknown, and yet known; as dying, and behold, we are alive; as chastened, and yet not put to death;
as sorrowful, and yet we always rejoice; as poor, and yet we make many rich; as having nothing, and yet we have everything.
Our mouth is opened to you, Corinthians, and our heart is enlarged.
You are not restricted by us; you are restricted by your own hearts.
In return, the same in exchange (I speak as to children): you too open wide your hearts.
Do not become yoke-mates with unbelievers: for what partnership is there between righteousness and lawlessness? Or what communion is there between light and darkness?
Or what agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever?
Or what accord does the temple of God have with idols? For you are temples of the living God, as God said: I will dwell and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Therefore come out from among them and separate yourselves, says the Lord, and do not touch what is unclean, and I will receive you.
"And I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters," says the Lord Almighty.
Since we have these promises, then, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, and let us bring holiness to completion in the fear of God.
Forgive us: we have harmed no one, we have corrupted no one, we have defrauded no one.
I do not say this to condemn you, for I said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
I have great confidence in you; I have great pride in you. I am filled with comfort; I overflow with joy in all our afflictions.
For when we came to Macedonia, our flesh had no relief at all, but we were afflicted in every way: outside, battles; inside, fears.
But God, who comforts the lowly, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
and not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted over you: he told us of your longing, your lamentation, your zeal for us, so that I rejoiced all the more.
For even if I grieved you with that letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it; I see that that letter grieved you, for a time.
Now I rejoice, not because you were grieved, but because you were grieved unto repentance; for you were grieved for God's sake, so that you might suffer no loss in anything through us.
For the grief that is from God produces a repentance of salvation that is not to be regretted, but the grief of this world produces death.

For behold, this very grief of yours from God: how much earnestness it produced among you, how much defense, how much indignation, how much fear, how much longing, how much zeal, how much vengeance, how much graciousness, or how much relief! In everything you have shown yourselves to be pure in that matter.
Although I wrote to you, it was surely not for the sake of the one who did wrong, nor of the one who was wronged, but so that your eagerness for us might be made manifest to you before God.
Therefore we are comforted in your comfort; and even more abundantly we rejoiced at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
For whatever I boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame; but just as I spoke everything to you in truth, so also our boasting to Titus has proved true.
And his compassion toward you is all the greater, as he remembers the obedience of all of you, how you received him with fear and trembling.
I rejoice, because in everything I have confidence in you.
And I make known to you, brothers, the grace of God that has been given to the churches of Macedonia,
For the great testing of affliction and their abundant joy and their deep poverty overflowed in the wealth of their generosity;
for according to their ability, I testify, and even beyond their ability, of their own free will,
with much entreaty they entreated us for the grace and the fellowship of the ministry to the saints.
And not only as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us by the will of God,
so that we should entreat Titus that, just as he had begun beforehand, so he should also complete this grace among you.
But just as you abound in everything, in faith and word and knowledge and all eagerness and in that love of ours among you, so may you abound in this grace too.
I do not speak to you by way of command, but by means of the eagerness of others [?] I am testing the sincerity of your love.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that for your sake he who was rich became poor, so that you might become rich through his poverty.
And for this reason I give you advice, for this is better for you, who began beforehand, since last year, not only to do but also to will.
But now, behold, complete the doing as well, so that just as there was eagerness for the willing, so there may also be completion out of what you have.
For if the eagerness is present, whatever a person has is acceptable as an offering, not what he does not have.
For it is not that others should have relief and you affliction, but that there should be equality.
At this present time your surplus is for their lack, so that their surplus may also be for your lack, that there may be equality.
As it is written: He who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little did not lack.
But thanks be to God, who put the same eagerness into the heart of Titus.
For he accepted the entreaty and, being more eager still, he went out to you of his own free will.
And with him we have sent the brother whose praise in the gospel is throughout all the churches,

and not only this, but he was also blessed by the laying on of hands by the churches as our companion in this grace, which is being ministered by us for the glory of the Lord himself and for the sake of your eagerness.
We are taking care about this, so that no one may blame us over this generous gift that we are administering.
For we plan in advance what is good, not only before the Lord but also before people.
And with them we have sent our brother, whom we have tested in many things many times and found eager, and who is now much more eager because of his great confidence in you.
Whether as regards Titus, our partner in the work and your helper, or our brothers, the apostles of the churches, the glories of Christ:
now therefore show them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you, before the face of the churches.
For concerning the ministry to the saints it is superfluous for me to write to you.
For I know your eagerness, about which I boasted of you among the Macedonians, saying that Achaia has been prepared since last year, and your zeal has stirred up many.
But I have sent the brothers so that our boasting about you may not be empty in this matter, so that, as I was saying, you may be prepared.
Lest perhaps, when Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we should be put to shame (not to say you) in this matter of boasting.

So I considered it better to entreat the brothers to go to you ahead of time, to prepare you beforehand, and to confirm your previously promised blessing [eulogia], so that it may be ready as a blessing and not as something extorted by greed.
But this I say: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows with blessing will also reap with blessing.
Let each one give as he has chosen in his heart, not with sorrow or unwillingly, for the Lord loves what is given with cheerfulness.
And God is able to make every necessary thing overflow for you, so that in everything and at all times you may have all things without lack and may abound in every good work.
As it is written: He scattered and gave to the poor, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.
May the one who gives seed to the sower and bread for food give to you as well. May he multiply your seed and increase the fruit of your righteousness.
may he enrich you in everything with all generosity, which through us produces thanksgiving to God.
For the ministry of this offering not only fills up the want of the saints, but also overflows through many in thanksgiving to God.
Through the proof given by this ministry you glorify God, by the submission of your confession to the gospel of Christ and by the generosity of your sharing with them and with all.
And in their prayer for you they long for you because of the surpassing grace of God that is upon you.
Thanks be to God for his inexpressible gifts.
I, Paul myself, entreat you by the meekness and goodness of Christ, I who am lowly among you when face to face, but when far away am bold toward you.
And I entreat you that I may not, when face to face, have to be bold with confidence, or think it right to be bold against certain people who consider us as walking according to the flesh.
For though we conduct ourselves in the flesh, we are not arrayed according to the flesh,
for the weapon of our warfare is not fleshly but powerful through God for the demolition of strongholds. We demolish reasonings
and every height raised up against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive into obedience to Christ,
and we hold ourselves ready to avenge all disobedience, when this obedience of yours is fulfilled.
Look at what is before each person's face. Whoever is confident of himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this again from himself: that just as he is Christ's, so also are we Christ's.
For if I should boast somewhat more about this authority of ours, which the Lord gave us for building you up and not for tearing you down, I would not be ashamed,
but I say this so that I may not be thought to be frightening you in some way by this letter.
For he says: These letters, it seems, are weighty and strong, but his coming in the body is weak and his speech contemptible.
Let such a person consider this: that as we are in the word of our letters when far away, so also are we in deed when near.

For we do not dare to judge ourselves among or compare ourselves with certain people who bear witness to themselves. But they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, and they do not understand.
But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the rule that God has apportioned to us, by that measure reaching even as far as you.
For we are not overextending ourselves, as though we had not reached you, for we came even as far as you with the gospel of Christ.
We do not boast beyond measure in another's labor, but we have hope that, as your faith grows, we will be greatly magnified among you according to our rule,
so as to preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, not to boast within another's rule of what is already prepared.
But whoever boasts, let him boast in the Lord.
For it is not the one who testifies for himself who is approved, but the one for whom the Lord testifies.
Would that you might bear with me in a little foolishness of mine; but indeed, do bear with me,
For I am zealous for you with the zeal of God, because I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a holy virgin.
But I am afraid that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so your minds may be corrupted from their sincerity toward Christ.
If someone comes and preaches another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or if he brings another spirit, which you did not receive, or another gospel, which you did not accept, you do well indeed.
For I think that I am in no way inferior to those super-apostles.
And though I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not in knowledge; rather, in everything we have been made manifest to you in all things.
Or did I commit some sin in humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you without payment?
I plundered other churches and took provisions in order to serve you; and when I came to you and was in need, I burdened none of you in anything.
For the brothers, when they came from Macedonia, supplied my need; and in everything I have kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will keep myself so.
The truth of Christ is with me, that this boast of mine will not be stopped in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
But what I am doing, I will also do, so that I may cut off the pretext, so that in that for which they want a pretext, so that in that of which they boast, they may be found just as we are.
For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, who transform themselves into apostles of Christ.
And it is no wonder, for the devil himself also transforms himself into an angel of light.
So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will be according to their deeds.
Again I say: let no one consider me foolish; but if not, then bear with me even as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
What I am saying, I am not saying from the Lord, but as if in foolishness, in this matter of boasting.
Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
For you gladly put up with fools, being wise yourselves.
For you put up with it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes from you, if someone exalts himself over you, if someone strikes you in the face.
I say this to your shame, that we, as it were, have been weak; but in whatever anyone dares to boast, I speak in foolishness, I too will dare.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? I speak still more foolishly: I am more so. In labor more, in torments more, in imprisonments beyond measure, in deaths many times.
From the Jews five times I received a beating of forty lashes less one.
Three times I was beaten with a rod, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, a night and a day I spent in the depths.

Journeys on the road many times, dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from kinsmen, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in cities, dangers in deserts, dangers on seas, dangers from false brothers,
in labor and toil, in sleepless watching many times, in hunger and thirst, in fasting many times, in cold and nakedness.
Besides all that, there is what comes upon me day after day: concern for all the churches.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
If boasting is necessary, I will boast of my weakness.
The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus the governor under King Aretas had surrounded the city of the Damascenes and wanted to seize me;
and through a window, in a basket, I was let down over the wall and escaped from his hands.
If boasting is necessary, it is not fitting for me, but I will come to the vision and revelation of the Lord.
I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago — whether in the body, I do not know, or whether without the body, I do not know, God knows — such a man was caught up as far as the third heaven.
And I know such a man — whether in the body or outside the body, I do not know, God knows —
that he was caught up into paradise and heard unutterable words, which it is not permitted for people to speak.
Of such a one I boast; but of myself I do not boast, except in my weaknesses.
But if I should wish to boast, I would not be foolish, for I would speak the truth; yet I refrain, lest anyone should credit to me more than what he sees in me or hears from me.
And so that I should not exalt myself through this excess of revelations, there was given to me a goad in the flesh — an angel of Satan — to torment me, so that I should not exalt myself.
And concerning this I implored the Lord three times, that he would remove it from me.

And he said to me: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." All the more gladly, therefore, will I boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, insults, afflictions, persecutions and hardships for Christ's sake, for when I become weak, then I become strong.
I have become foolish in boasting, for you compelled me. For you ought to have testified on my behalf, since I fell short in nothing of those great apostles, even though I am nothing.
Indeed, the sign of the apostle was performed among you with all patience, with signs and wonders and power.
For what is there in which you were worsted more than the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you at all? Forgive me this wrong.

Behold, now for the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not burden you at all, for I do not seek what is yours, but you. For children do not store up treasure for their parents, but parents for their children.
And I will gladly spend and be utterly spent for your souls; the more I love you, the less you love me.
But let it be so: I myself did not burden you; yet, being shrewd, I took you by guile.
Did I perhaps take advantage of you through any of those I sent to you?
I entreated Titus and sent the brother along with him. Did Titus steal anything from you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not follow in the same footsteps?
Again you think that we are making our defense to you. We speak before God in Christ, and everything, beloved, is for your building up.

For I fear that perhaps when I come I may not find you as I wish, and that I may be found by you as you do not wish; that perhaps there may be among you strife and envy, outbursts of anger, slanders, factions, arrogance, insolence, and disorders.

I fear that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and that I may mourn over many of those who sinned beforehand and did not repent of the impurity, fornication, and filthiness that they committed.
Behold, I am coming to you for the third time. By the mouth of two and three witnesses every word is established.

I said it before and I say it beforehand now as well, as when I was present the second time, and now from afar I write to those who sinned beforehand and to all the others: if I come again, I will no longer spare them,
since you are seeking proof of him who speaks through me, Christ, who is not weak toward you but is powerful among you.
For even though he was crucified in weakness, yet he lives by the power of God; and we too are weak toward him, but we shall live with him by the power of God, together with you.
Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith. Examine yourselves. Or do you not know yourselves, that Jesus Christ is among you? Unless perhaps you are somehow untested and unproven.
But I hope that you will come to know that we are not unproven.
And I pray to God that he may do you no evil, not so that we may appear proven, but so that you may do good, even if we are as though unproven.
For we have no power to speak evil against the truth, but only on behalf of the truth.
For we rejoice whenever we are weak and you are strong; for this too we pray, that you may be made firm.
And for this reason I write these things from afar, so that when I come I may not act unsparingly, according to the authority that the Lord has given me for building up and not for tearing down.
From now on, brothers, rejoice, be strengthened, be comforted, give comfort, be of the same mind, make peace; and may the God of love and peace be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God the Father, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with all of you. Amen.
